span.label: when a classifier trained on one distribution can be expected to work on another, and how to weight source against target data when a little labelled target data exists
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: what quantity, estimable from unlabeled samples, bounds the target error of a source-trained classifier
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: a classifier-induced divergence that can be estimated from finite unlabeled samples, and a bound in which the target error is the source error plus that divergence plus the error of the ideal joint hypothesis
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanism
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: domain adaptation - training where the labels are and deploying where they are not, with a theory whose usable half is the half that can be computed without labels
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: a VC-style uniform convergence argument, with the domain distance defined as a supremum over the hypothesis class and computed by training a classifier to separate unlabeled source from unlabeled target instances
span.term: a VC-style uniform convergence argument, with the domain distance defined as a supremum over the hypothesis class and computed by training a classifier to separate unlabeled source from unlabeled target instances
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the L1 divergence takes a supremum over all measurable subsets and is rejected as unestimable and over-strict; the H-divergence takes it over the hypothesis class. So the distance between two FIXED distributions is a function of H - a richer class sees the domains as further apart, and the bound loosens because the model got more expressive rather than because the data moved
span.term: a distance defined by the classifier you were going to use
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: label every unlabeled source instance 0 and every unlabeled target instance 1, train a classifier to tell them apart, and read the divergence off its error. If the domains are indistinguishable to H the divergence is zero. The measurement IS the adversary, which is why the whole domain-adversarial literature follows from this paragraph
span.term: measure the difference by trying to detect it
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: target error is bounded by source error plus divergence plus lambda. The first two come from unlabeled data. Lambda is the error of the best joint hypothesis and needs labelled target data to evaluate - the thing the setting is defined by not having. THE BOUND IS USABLE EXACTLY WHEN ITS UNCHECKABLE TERM IS SMALL
span.term: the third term is the assumption
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: two domains can differ in their labeling functions as well as in their input distributions. One clause - `since we expect the labeling function difference to be small in practice` - removes the first from the theory. Everything downstream measures distributional shift and inherits the assumption without restating it
span.term: the half of the difference that is assumed away
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: computing the H-divergence needs the minimum-error hypothesis for the source-versus-target problem, which is intractable for most classes. What is used instead is the error of a hypothesis minimising a convex upper bound - so the reported divergence is an approximation of an approximation, and the paper says so
span.term: an intractable quantity approximated by a surrogate
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the bound is only useful when the ideal joint hypothesis has small error, and that error cannot be estimated without labelled target data
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the difference between the two domains' labeling functions is assumed small rather than measured
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: minimising error to compute the H-divergence is computationally intractable for most hypothesis classes, so a convex surrogate is used
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: common divergences such as L1 and Kullback-Leibler cannot be accurately estimated from finite samples in a distribution-free setting
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: with enough labelled target data the source data is never preferred, no matter how much of it there is - the method's value is bounded by target-label scarcity
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the practical recommendation holds only given a reasonable measure of complexity
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: a divergence built for change detection in data streams, taken into statistical learning theory as the domain-distance term of a generalisation bound
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: binary classification itself used as a measuring instrument - a discriminator trained to separate two unlabeled samples, with its error read as a distance
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the H-divergence checked against the L1 divergence on both counts that matter - estimability from finite samples and tightness of the resulting bound
span.note: eliminates: a new measure adopted for convenience - it is shown never to be larger than the one it replaces, so the bound cannot have been loosened to make it work · outcome: held

span.label: the bound's behaviour examined at both extremes of lambda rather than only where it is convenient
span.note: eliminates: a bound that is quietly vacuous when adaptation is impossible - the paper states plainly that a large lambda means no classifier serves both domains · outcome: held

span.label: the intractability of computing the H-divergence stated, with the convex surrogate named as an approximation rather than presented as the quantity
span.note: eliminates: a reported divergence being read as the defined one - the gap between them is declared at the point the substitution is made · outcome: held

span.label: source domains at varying distance compared against target-only training as labelled target data increases
span.note: eliminates: the claim that source data always helps - with enough target labels it never does, whatever its volume · outcome: failed
